source_text: Si quis dicit carnem Christi homoousion, id est consubstantialem esse divinitati, et non confitetur ipsum in forma Dei et Deum esse ante saecula, et seipsum exinanisse, et formam servi accepisse sicut scriptum est, anathema sit. Quomodo autem caro post tempus homoousios, id est eiusdem substantiae, cum sempiterna divinitate dici potest? Homoousion enim dicitur quod est idem natura et eadem sempiternitate invariabiliter.
thought_title: The flesh is not consubstantial with the divinity
orientation: Gregory is closing his treatise with a final anathema against saying Christ's flesh is consubstantial with the divinity.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says the flesh of Christ is homoousion, that is, consubstantial with the divinity, and does not confess that he himself was in the form of God and was God before the ages, and that he emptied himself, and that he accepted the form of a servant, as it is written, let him be anathema. But how can flesh in time be called homoousios, that is, of the same substance, with the eternal divinity? For homoousion is said of that which is the same in nature and in the same eternal existence unchangeably.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'consubstantial' for homoousion; banned rendering is 'of the same substance'.
The Latin glosses homoousion with consubstantialem; glossary requires 'consubstantial'.
Echoes Philippians 2:6; 'form' is the glossary term for forma.
Glossary requires 'form of a servant' for forma servi.
Keeps the temporal contrast with 'after time'; 'sempiternal' preserves the Latin sempiterna.

bible_refs.note: in forma Dei ... exinanisse ... formam servi accepisse

pass_b_english: If anyone says that the flesh of Christ is consubstantial with the divinity, and does not confess that he himself was in the form of God and was God before the ages, and that he emptied himself and took the form of a servant, as it is written, let him be anathema. For how can flesh that exists after time be called consubstantial with the sempiternal divinity? What is consubstantial is what is the same in nature and in sempiternity, without change.

last_rejected.why: "post tempus" means "after a time/after some time" (temporal, created), not "after time" (metaphysical/atemporal).
last_rejected.fix: flesh that exists in time or after a beginning
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'post tempus' literally means 'after time'; rendering as 'exists after time' captures the source's temporal-vs-sempiternal contrast adequately.
